description.narrative:
Stakeholder effects Access to Trade Finance for Issuing Banks and Traders: Issuing Banks (IBs) in Emerging Markets and Developing Economies (EMDE) face ongoing challenges in the availability of financing to support their customers, who are traders exporting or importing commodities (including critical goods such as food and energy products). GTFP provides trade finance support to these IBs and their trade finance customers by providing IFCs guarantee through risk mitigation to their counterparty banks and thereby making these trade-flows happen. These guarantees are especially critical to support trade for lower income and fragile and conflict-affected countries, where the risks are perceived to be higher and likely have very few (if any) global CBs willing to participate. GTFP allocates line limits to each IB in the program. IBs utilize/draw upon IFC guarantee whenever they have a trade transaction for which CBs require IFC guarantee for the transaction to happen. Therefore, by definition, each of the transactions booked under GTFP would not have happened without GTFP participation. These individual transactions cumulatively have large impact for these EMDEs to continue to trade and raise their income/GDP.
Market Creation - Integration GTFP improves overall market integration by (1) maintaining and expanding trade finance, financial linkages and trade across multiple markets through strengthening these bilateral correspondent banking connections; (2) the program itself that serves an enabling platform to make new connections between local and international banks and their customers; (3) channeling new sources of capital to support EMDE trade flow through demonstration and replication of successful correspondent banking connections and the trade finance program itself as a successful investment instrument. Such a network is critical to help maintain access to finance in markets that are experiencing cross-border retrenchment.

The proposed project is an unfunded trade finance facility under IFCs Global Trade Finance Program (GTFP) of up to US$30 million for Banco Macro S.A. (Banco Macro or the Bank). The trade line will support the Banks short-term trade finance transactions by offering confirming banks partial or full guarantees to cover payment risk of the Bank in Argentina.
